instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I marked our bedroom floor with crosses like the builder. We wanted a home we made together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His crosses mark rotten boards to remove. You've marked the entire bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making room for us. We can start where the bed will go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't sleep in there until it's repaired. We'll have to share the tent in the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then that's our first room. Bring both pillows; we can plan the bedroom with our heads together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I pulled the plug when the sound man did. This concert was meant to bring the village together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged a faulty microphone. You unplugged the stage supply, lights and sound together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the sound. We'll hear each other sing now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half the audience has gone home for torches. They want to read the song sheets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask them to light a neighbour's sheet as well as their own. That's the village together, even before the chorus.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've wrapped your teacup like Mary wrapped hers. Take it; remember our afternoons wherever you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mary was wrapping a cracked cup for the bin. I'm only walking home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, packing to last. Keep yours where you can see it when you've settled somewhere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring it back tomorrow. We can have tea then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the matching saucer too. If you don't make it back, I want you to have our tea together, wherever you are.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed six lunches like the coach driver. You'll be well fed when you leave us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His lunches are for six passengers. I'm visiting my sister in the next town for one afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, plenty to share. Give her one with my love, and keep the others for whatever comes after.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm coming back on the four o'clock bus. Keep dinner for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wrap your favourite dinner too. Then you'll have something of home even if the four o'clock is the last bus you take this way.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed out the fare like the taxi driver. The lift costs petrol and an explanation for three weeks of silence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His cross cancelled a fare. Are you cancelling the petrol money?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, adjusting the account. Petrol's still due, and now tell me why money was the only part you heard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay it. Can we talk about the silence on the way instead of here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Petrol, the three weeks, and why you couldn't face saying it at my door. Keep the radio off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed out the dress price like the shop assistant. Ten pounds to borrow it, plus an apology for calling it hideous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She crossed out a price because the zip was broken. Is yours broken too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, condition checked. The zip works. Ten pounds, and say you were wrong about my taste.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty. I'll tell everyone tonight that you chose it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep ten. Tell them you laughed when I chose it, too. I want the compliment with its history attached.

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One box to the van, agreed. I've ticked this one like you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My ticks mark empty boxes. The full ones are over by the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, checking the supply. Choose my one full box, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take the big one. Then bring it back empty so we can fill it with the books still on the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One box to the van, not back to the shelf. Choose what goes in it before I lift it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I agreed to watch your dog today. I've put his bowl away like you did, so we're finishing up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I put it away before his medicine, not at bedtime. My train won't get in until after midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, clearing for the next stage. Today still ends at midnight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My brother can collect him at eleven, but he'd have to bring him back here while he goes to the station for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eleven is today; bringing him back isn't in our sentence. Ask your brother to take him to the station too.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the hall key in my teacup like you. The wedding invitation can sit underneath; everything for getting in, together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cup was empty. Yours still has tea in it, and the key's dropped to the bottom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, all in one place. Use the invitation to dry the key when you fish it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The paper's stuck in the key's teeth. I can peel it away, but the printed address is coming off with it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the address to me before you peel. Then put the clean key in the empty cup; I'll have to carry the invitation in my head.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took away a chair like the caterer did. The cake can sit on the piano stool, and your uncle can have the window seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She took away a broken chair. You've removed the only spare seat for the pianist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making a little room. The pianist can sit at the window until we're ready for music.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Uncle's there, leaning against the window. He has to move so I can open it; the cake's icing is melting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring my chair back for Uncle. Then open his window for the cake, and I'll hold the cake while the pianist takes the stool.
